method: Direct original-image observation only. Pixel positions below are approximate visual observations, not extracted coordinates or candidate requirements.

items.observation: Two side-by-side arrangements on white: a compact left arrangement and a wider right arrangement. The left caption is a lower-case a-shaped glyph; the right caption is the Cyrillic be-shaped glyph (U+0431). They sit below the arrangements. No surrounding box, graph, table, numbered points, angle marks or numeric values are visible.

A vertical, dark/hatched elongated body extends approximately from y=68 to y=276, around x=79..103. Short horizontal outlined caps or plates at both ends extend to the right, approximately x=76..128 at the top and x=73..129 at the bottom. The end plates are horizontal and mutually parallel; the long body is vertical and connects their left/central portion.

A separate straight vertical ink line around x=47 connects the upper and lower end levels, to the left of the body. It carries an upward arrowhead near the top and a downward arrowhead near the bottom. A small italic length-symbol-like glyph appears farther left near mid-height (around x=20,y=164). The source glyph is provisionally read as l; prose has not yet been inspected to resolve whether this line is the bidirectional light path, dimension marking, or both.

The right arrangement begins with a solid dark/hatched vertical body around x=236..258, y=67..274. Horizontal upper and lower caps extend approximately x=234..282. Their levels and orientation closely match the left apparatus. The source does not draw an additional separate initial vertical ray alongside this solid body.

A short horizontal arrow above the solid right-panel apparatus points to the right (approximately x=244..276,y=46). An italic v-shaped symbol is above it. This explicitly supplies a rightward direction associated with that apparatus.

A dashed vertical elongated outline at approximately x=335..359 is capped by short horizontal dashed/outlined end plates at y=61..74 and y=275..286, extending to x=388..390. It is to the right of the solid initial apparatus and retains the same upright shape, horizontal cap orientation and approximately the same upper/lower levels.

A second dashed vertical elongated outline is farther right, around x=439..465. Short horizontal dashed/outlined caps occupy approximately x=436..488 at y=57..69 and y=271..284. This is another rightward displacement of the same upright arrangement; its vertical levels are approximately aligned with the earlier caps. Scan imperfections must not be mistaken for deliberate height changes.

A solid diagonal rises rightward from approximately (271,275), on the right portion of the initial lower plate, to approximately (372,70), on the right portion of the middle upper plate. A prominent arrowhead on the lower/middle part of this segment points up and right.

A solid diagonal leaves the same middle upper contact and descends rightward to approximately (474,272), on the final lower plate. Its prominent arrowhead points down and right. It and the ascending leg form an inverted V with a shared upper contact; both span the same approximate vertical separation and have approximately equal opposing slopes/equal horizontal advances.

At the final lower contact, a short further solid segment turns up and right toward approximately (493,224), with an up-right arrowhead. It indicates the continuation after the lower reflection, not a third complete equal-height leg or a fourth full apparatus snapshot.

The principal light contacts occur on horizontal end plates: initial lower contact, middle upper contact, final lower contact. The direction reverses vertically at each retained bounce while continuing rightward. The lower contacts flank the upper contact horizontally; both complete legs meet the same upper contact without a gap. The dashed bodies are later positions of one similarly shaped apparatus rather than multiple independent instruments. No ray is drawn through an opaque body; each contact is on an exposed portion of an end plate to its right.

Only the two panel captions, the length-like symbol and the speed-like symbol are visible. No c, times, mirror names, observer labels, theta, path lengths, coordinate axes, colors or explanatory sentences are printed inside the image. Solid initial apparatus, dashed later apparatus, solid directed paths and body hatching are meaningful distinctions. Ragged strokes, inconsistent outline thickness and old-book texture are not independent physical objects.
